clue.text: Wave unfortunate in front of ship

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
ill, as in ill luck, means unfortunate

explanation.surface: Someone waves, unluckily, at the front of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of ship' reads as a position phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'front of ship' is the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a great swelling sea wave.

clue.text: Teasing appears damaging, in time

parts.note: bad, as in bad for you, means damaging
taken as written
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Some mockery is starting to look harmful over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, witty banter, a synonym for good-humoured teasing.

clue.text: US city streets unprepared for camel's back-breaker?

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
ST is the abbreviation for street, so two of them for the plural
raw food is unprepared, not yet cooked

explanation.surface: An American city's roads are too rough to carry a camel's load.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom: it is the straw that breaks the camel's back, the final small burden that causes collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the final small extra burden that causes collapse, as the proverbial straw did to the camel.

clue.text: Instrument extracting odd parts of comb honey

indicators.note: removing the odd-numbered letters of comb honey leaves just its even letters

explanation.surface: An instrument draws out bits of honey from the comb.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Growing, and pretty

explanation.definitionFit: Becoming means coming to be, as in growing into something; it also means attractive or flattering, as a becoming dress.

clue.text: Serious home for an organ?

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A grave question about where a body part might live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a church instrument, but here it is a body part, the ear, and its home a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and grave in intention, a synonym for serious.

clue.text: Alumnus learned to use an eraser?

parts.note: an OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
literate means educated, well read

explanation.surface: A former pupil, well schooled, rubs things out.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is a British term for a school's former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out completely, which rubbing with an eraser does to pencil marks.

clue.text: British isle takes on an inhabitant of Des Moines, perhaps

parts.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British island takes in a visitor from the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Des Moines is the capital of the US state of Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Des Moines resident is an example of someone from that Midwest state.

clue.text: Is one ordered to be a supporter?

definitions.text: Is one ordered to be a supporter?

parts.words: Is one ordered to be a supporter?
parts.note: the senior English order of chivalry bears the name of a band that holds up a stocking, so one belongs to an order and is a supporter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if they are being told to back a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' suggests commanded; it means belonging to an Order of chivalry, and 'supporter' is a stocking band, not a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A band worn to hold up stockings, which also names the oldest British order of knighthood.

clue.text: Month before sign of winter, one's green

parts.note: NOV is November
ice appears in winter

explanation.surface: Before winter's frost, in late autumn, a beginner turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner or learner is inexperienced, which is what being green means.

clue.text: Where flashing lights darken, do they do this?

parts.note: a disco is a club with flashing coloured lights
to lour is to darken or look threatening, as a sky does

explanation.surface: A question whether strobes in a dim nightclub stain things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition asks whether the flashing lights change the colour of things around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To discolour is to change or spoil the colour of something, which coloured lights appear to do.

clue.text: Cow more inclined towards the grass?

explanation.definitionFit: To lower is to frown or scowl, and a cow is one that moos; also it means nearer the ground, as one inclines downwards.

clue.text: Food without gagging order?

parts.note: no means none, without any
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A newspaper story printed free of any injunction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for grub or a meal.

clue.text: Poet's written about individual, European dabbler in the arts

indicators.note: the poet's name is written around the other letters

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
I, the Roman numeral one, means a single individual
a Lett is a Latvian

explanation.surface: A poet has written about one person, a European amateur in the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' wraps the poet's name around the inserted letters, which sit after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante is an amateur who takes up art superficially.

clue.text: Players helping with man's personal loss

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a play
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Actors share out food while one of them suffers a private setback.
explanation.definitionFit: Castration removes the testes, a very personal loss for a male.

clue.text: English follows other language, as relevant

indicators.note: follows puts the English letter after the language

parts.note: German is a language other than English

explanation.surface: English is learnt after another tongue, as it is relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means pertinent or closely connected to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Sixty minutes feeding behind bird

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the hour is put inside the rear

parts.note: tush is slang for the backside
HR is the abbreviation for an hour

explanation.surface: An hour spent feeding a bird from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word but is a noun, the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The song thrush is a common speckled songbird.

clue.text: Conversation between Doc and Sneezy, perhaps?

explanation.definitionFit: Small talk is light social chatter; it is also what passes between two of Snow White's dwarves, little people.

clue.text: Shade match through enclosure

indicators.note: through puts one word inside the other, running through it

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
to agree is to match or correspond

explanation.surface: A fence's colour matches the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale bright yellowish green, a colour or tint.

clue.text: Control urge to visit Cornwall?

indicators.note: to visit puts the urge beside the region it travels to

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west, SW, of England
an itch is a restless urge

explanation.surface: A desire to travel to Cornwall for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the far south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a device for controlling electrical circuits.

clue.text: Pick up information about the plant

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for picking up news wraps the article

parts.note: to hear is to receive news

explanation.surface: Someone gathers facts on a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it is a container signal; 'the' is used literally as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a low shrub with purple flowers growing on moors.

clue.text: Daily struggle beginning to rankle a bit

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the opening letter of rankle

parts.note: a trace is a small amount, a bit

explanation.surface: A daily grind starts to irritate somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the exhausting competitive routine of working life.

clue.text: Rising road rage rarely receives respect

indicators.note: Rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
receives means the words take in and hold the answer within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Road rage seldom earns anyone esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'receives respect' as the definition, leaving the hidden word without an indicator; 'receives' is that indicator. In a down clue 'Rising' means read upwards, turning DRAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Regard as a noun is esteem or high opinion, the same as respect.

clue.text: A pole held by limb a shade above the window

indicators.note: held by means contained inside, so the pole sits inside the limb

parts.note: a wing is a bird's limb
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A pole is held up by an arm to give shade over a window.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas cover that shades a window or shopfront.

clue.text: Wave moving forth and back on Silver State in Australian city

parts.note: to wag is to wave to and fro

indicators.note: moving forth and back says the wave goes one way, then a second copy is turned round

parts.note: to wag is to wave to and fro
AG is the chemical symbol for silver
GA is the abbreviation for Georgia, a US state

explanation.surface: A wave rolls to and fro across Nevada, the Silver State, near a Sydney suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving forth and back' turns the second WAG into GAW. 'Silver State' looks like Nevada's nickname, but splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagga Wagga is a large inland city in New South Wales.

clue.text: In which The Ashes celebrated audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the word for famous is heard, not seen

parts.note: great means famous, celebrated

explanation.surface: The cricket trophy series is cheered loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series; here they are simply fireside ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A grate is the metal frame in a fireplace where burnt cinders collect.

clue.text: Colours fade

explanation.definitionFit: Colours are a regimental banner or standard; to flag is to tire or weaken.

clue.text: One's gaining entry to US state-given this?

indicators.note: gaining entry to means going inside, so the letters go into the state

parts.note: VA is Virginia
I is one, and 's is is

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether a state will let them in.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is the endorsement that allows a foreigner to enter a country.

clue.text: Asian artist joining queue, say, between uprights

indicators.note: between puts the letters inside the pair of uprights

parts.note: the letter I is shaped like an upright post, so two of them
RA is a Royal Academician
the letter Q is pronounced like queue

explanation.surface: A painter from Asia joins a line between goalposts.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a person from Iraq in western Asia.

clue.text: Raunchier gyrating gives you very bad wind

indicators.note: gyrating means whirling round, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A dancer moving lewdly brings on a storm of flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical storm with fierce gales.

clue.text: Leaves retired Frenchman in dull coat

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed name goes inside the colour
coat means the colour wraps around the name

parts.note: grey means dull, cheerless

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A French pensioner sheds his drab jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the French name into ENER, which the drab colour then coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is foliage, plants collectively.

clue.text: Fastener securing ship's cake

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the fastener wraps the vessel

parts.note: a pin fastens things
Noah's ark is a ship

explanation.surface: A clip holds the boat's cake in place.
explanation.walkthrough: PARKIN is a sticky oatmeal and treacle gingerbread from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a ginger cake made with oatmeal and treacle.
